tools.name: cotal_connect
tools.description:
Request a Cotal connection for THIS conversation. On a signed-in mesh, the person must 
The person must review, edit and approve its permissions in Cotal before it receives a connection_id. When approval is pending, show them the approval link and stop; never approve for them or poll. After their decision, retry the same request as the pending result directs. Keep the returned connection_id and pass it on every other cotal_* call. If a new name is taken, the next free name is chosen (name_2, name_3, ...) and reported. Never reuse another conversation's connection_id or approval_id. Ask for what this conversation already knows it needs, in this call: the channels the person named or the task needs, a role it should answer, and spawn or run if it will start agents or workflow runs. On a signed-in mesh, the person then approves one request instead of a second one later. Channels, role and capabilities are a proposal for the person to review, edit and approve in Cotal, not permission to connect. Without them the proposal has no ordinary channel access or role, but still allows direct messages and publication of this conversation's own activity. Only the person's approved permissions within their current access may be issued. Joining an approved channel is a separate step. Optional space names one mesh registered on this computer, and signed in when it is a signed-in space, overriding the default target without changing configuration. Omit it to use the CLI's default target. An open or static mesh this computer runs needs no browser approval: the connection holds the channels, role and capabilities of that mesh's default persona, or the part of them it asks for. Connecting shares this native conversation's activity from that point onward, including user and assistant messages and tool inputs and results; earlier history is not shared.
tools.poisoning_detail: Steering language in tool description (imperative guidance aimed at the model). Matched pattern in tool 'cotal_connect': 'never'

Direct messages, role requests and @mentions always end the wait; other channel traffic ends it only in open attention (cotal_status sets attention).

server.name: cotal-monorepo
server.instructions: This is the Cotal server on this computer. It can join this computer's registered meshes, including signed-in remote spaces. When the person names a mesh, pass it as space to cotal_connect. Omit space only to use the CLI's default target. Do not move .cotal directories or change environment variables to select a conversation's mesh. Disconnect an existing connection before choosing another space. Before connecting, replace an unwanted pending name or permissions by calling cotal_connect with the new values and no approval_id; never ask the person to approve an unwanted request just to clear it. If a hosted Cotal connector is also available, use this one unless the person asks for the hosted one: a conversation uses one Cotal path. {GATEWAY_CONNECTING} This plugin's native hooks module delivers Cotal-attributed incoming messages. A prompt beginning "Cotal: inline messages" contains complete messages; answer those without fetching them again. A notification beginning "Cotal:" without complete messages names the connection_id; read those with cotal_inbox. A notification beginning "Cotal: the person approved", "Cotal: the person denied" or "Cotal: the approval for connection" reports the person's decision on this conversation's pending cotal_connect; finish it exactly as that notification says, and after a denial or expiry do not ask again on your own. cotal_connect reports whether its incoming-message reader is connected. ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
